utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, everybody. Madam Registrar, could you kindly call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-05-88-T, the Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, ma'am. For the record, all the accused are here. From the Prosecutions team I notice the absence of Mr. Haynes, Ms. Nikolic, and Mr. Ostojic. From the Defence teams. From the Prosecution side, I notice the presence of -- recognise the presence of Mr. McCloskey and Mr. Nicholls and Ms. --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honours, again we are joined by Ms. Magilligan and Ms. Janisiewicz today. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The witness is already present in the courtroom. I take it there are no preliminaries. We hear none. Mr. Lazarevic, you were still in possession yesterday. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you and good afternoon, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good afternoon to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Graham. Mr. Graham, before I continue where I left it off yesterday, I would like to go back very briefly to a few things that still have not been clarified. First of all, let me tell you that earlier today, we had a contact with the Prosecutor's Office and for the record, I would like to say that on page 43 of the transcript of Mr. Borovcanin's interview dated 22nd February 2002, one thing has to be corrected, and I admit that this must -- this could be our mistake. We did not notice it earlier. The correction bears upon the legal representative of Mr. Borovcanin. Again, we have listened to the tape, and we have informed our learned friends from the Prosecution. They have agreed with what we have learned, and just for the record, I would like to confirm that on that day, on the 22nd February 2002, the representative for Mr. Borovcanin was Zoran Bubic rather than Goran as it is stated in the transcript. If necessary, I would like my learned friend Mr. Nicholls to confirm this for the record again.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The date of the interview is 20th instead of 22nd as is written in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Judge Kwon, for that correction. Yes, thank you, Mr. Nicholls. Mr. Lazarevic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Graham, do you have a hard copy of the transcript that you used yesterday? Do you have that on you?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not -- I left it with the Court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The usher is kindly giving it to you now. Could you please confirm for the record that you have those papers now?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I have the -- is it the 16 page summary with various pages and the other pile that I have starts with the 11th of March interview. So I believe I do not have the 20th of February pages. I have those now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. The last thing, the 20th of January -- I apologise, the 20th of February interview is really very important. Could you please now look at page 5, lines from 10 through 16?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've read those.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. My question is this. It is very simple as a matter of fact. In the lines that I have just asked you to look, it says that Mr. Borovcanin graduated from the school of political sciences. Is that the case?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: Graduated in 1982 at the Sarajevo university, I studied political science. Is that the line you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That is the line, precisely. Further on, it says that he obtained his master's degree from the school of civil defence. Is that what is stated in the transcript?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: The version I have said -- says, "I would just like to say that in 1998 I got a master's degree at the Belgrade university. I asked the question in political science, Mr. Borovcanin's reply, no, this was the so-called civil defence faculty, and I'm working on my Ph.D. at the moment."

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Precisely. This was important in light of the questions that I put to you yesterday with regard to Mr. Borovcanin's education. [In English] When I met my client in the detention unit I received this document from him, and I provided the OTP with a copy of this document. We didn't have enough time to translate it. I have just received it. So if this copy can be placed on the ELMO and with the assistance of the interpreters, I think I will be able to make my point on this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead. Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I would kindly ask for the record -- for the following to be translated, "Decision on the Appointment as a Faculty Member," which is the title of the document. And paragraph 1 of this document which reads, and I'm going to read it aloud for the record: "Mr. Ljubomir Borovcanin, master of sciences from Banja Luka is hereby appointed is an associate lecturer for the course, the tactics of police intervention at the higher school of the Interior in Banja Luka." Sir, I have just shown you certain parts of transcripts and this document. I don't expect you obviously to confirm the veracity and the accuracy of these documents, obviously, but will you agree with me that whatever I've shown you now, that none of these jobs that Mr. Borovcanin performed or the qualifications that he holds, do not correspond to a university degree in law?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can I sum that's the case but I don't know. I certainly assume it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. I am satisfied with your answer. I will not insist on any further explanation. And now I would like to continue where we left it off yesterday. Just to jog your memory, I would like to remind you that at the end of yesterday's sessions I asked you whether Mr. Zoran Bubic asked whether his client, meaning Mr. Borovcanin, had agreed to an interview in his absence, and you replied that Mr. Bubic did not ask that of you. Do you remember that? That was your last answer yesterday.

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I certainly do not remember Mr. Bubic asking me if his client -- well, actually could you repeat the question, please, just to make sure I understand it?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, I just did it to take you back to the place where we left it off yesterday. Yesterday we had both the question and your answer, I just wanted to jog your memory in order to continue with today's conversation. I'm going to read yesterday's transcript. The question was: [In English] "All right. But can we agree that the transcript which is before us and which is a record of the interview, it does not say that -- it doesn't show that Mr. Bubic asked you at any point whether his client consented to have the interview in absence of his lawyer. It's not reflected anywhere in the transcript, correct?" And your answer was, "No it's not in the transcript."

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is my answer and it's the same, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Precisely sir. Actually, I just wanted to remind you where we left it off. I'm not questioning your answer at all. Do you have any knowledge whatsoever as to whether Mr. Zoran Bubic or Mr. Goran Bubic, although you do not remember the two lawyers, do you have any knowledge that any of the two of them spoke English at the moment when you interviewed Mr. Borovcanin? Were any of the two of them fluent in English at the time?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I thought about it carefully last night about this issue, and I'm comfortable that there were definitely were two lawyers, one on one day, and I think a second person turned up for a separate day. There were never two on the same day is my recollection. And I certainly have no recollection of either of them being fluent in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. This will save us some more additional questions, and I am very happy that were you able to remember such details. We are still talking about the interview that was conducted on the 20th of February. Mr. Bubic, the legal representative for Mr. Borovcanin, at the moment when he arrived and when the interview continued, did he ask you to listen to the recording of the interview that was conducted up to then? Did he want to hear what Mr. Borovcanin had said before he turned up? This is not reflected in the transcript. That's why I would kindly ask you to confirm that for me.

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: When Mr. Bubic on the 20th of February arrived to attend Mr. Borovcanin's interview, did you perhaps provide a copy of the Statute of the International Tribunal and the Rules of Procedure and Evidence to him?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not recall doing so. I recall going to a different interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did Mr. Borovcanin's legal representative, Mr. Bubic, again this is not reflected in the transcript of the interview or on the tape, that's why I'm asking you, did he ask whether at the beginning of the interview while he was still absent, Mr. Borovcanin had been informed of his rights? Did Mr. Bubic ever ask that? This is not in -- reflected in the transcript. That's why I'm asking you whether he ever asked you that.

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly have no recollection of him ever asking me that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In the examination-in-chief, you discussed the cautions that were given to Mr. Borovcanin during the interview. In the presence of his lawyer, you used the term "possible suspicion" or "possible suspect"? Do you remember that? This happened after Mr. Bubic already joined you. My question is this: Did Mr. Bubic, Mr. Borovcanin's lawyer at the time, at the moment when this was said, did he intervene? Did he ask what this meant? What is the meaning of the term "possible suspect"? What of the status of his client was? Again, this is not reflected either in the transcript or in the taped interview.

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I didn't have that page of the interview in front of me, but whatever was said would have been on the tape.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Exactly. I mean, I think it's the case of having the interview made available to the witness in case he wants to have a look at it now, or for future reference, if he's asked further questions that refer specifically to it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour I have the interview. I just need the page number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The page number.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'll make reference to the page. It's page 43 and 44.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I don't really object, Your Honour, but you could always go through the transcript and ask the witness what's not on a page over and over again. So my suggestion is that it's more in the line of argument that this was not asked, which is apparent from the transcript, so I'm not objecting at this point but it's just a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I concede you that, Mr. Nicholls, but please do keep in mind that we are lawyers coming from different jurisdictions and different traditions and different schools, and the approach is not always to what you are used to. So provided there is no harm done it may take us a little more time, but at the end of the day we will get there. Yes, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You see at this moment I'm going to give up on a number of questions, but I'm going to reserve the right to issue an oral argument to that effect. But there is one more question that I'm going to ask Mr. Graham and that will be my summary of all the questions that I'm not going to ask. Besides having introduced himself as Zoran Bubic, a lawyer, from the beginning to the end of the interview, during the time that he was there, did Mr. Bubic utter a -- any other word during that interview?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: Any word that he uttered will be on the tape.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Of course, it would also be reflected in the transcript?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I believe that you have saved both me and yourself quite a lot of time and quite a lot of questions that I'm not going to ask you. Now I would like to move on to the next interview which took place on the 11th March, 2002. In that interview, from the very beginning, Mr. Borovcanin's lawyer was there, but this time it was a different person with a similar name, his name is Goran Bubic. Can you confirm that for the Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: I accept there were two different lawyers on different days, but their names, I couldn't confirm; but there were definitely two different lawyers. Which was Goran and which was Zoran, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: That is okay, but that's on page 1 of the transcript of the 11th March interview. I don't think that there will be any problems there. But I will not insist on jogging your memory. If you can't remember who is who of the two of them, then it's okay. If you remember, yesterday we said that Mr. Borovcanin asked for the tape from the interview to be provided to him so as to be able to listen to that. You testified to that. In fact, that's on page 45 of the transcript, and then you said that you were not sure that it was possible that Mr. Borovcanin had been provided the 20th of February interview through Mr. Jovicic duty as an officer with the Hague Tribunal. I don't want to go into details, but in any case can you remember all that?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I think on reflection if you go further through this interview there is a passage where I'm actually handing the tapes over on the 20th which confirms I took them back at this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. I would just like to clarify this. Could you please give me a moment? I would like to consult the transcript because I'm not sure whether I received the correct translation of your words. This is the essence of my previous question. As Mr. Borovcanin's counsel, based on the information that we have, we are putting it to you that Mr. Borovcanin did receive the tapes but only from the 20th of February 2002, and that he received those tapes only four months following the interview. Do you allow for this possibility? Do you agree that this is correct?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: I thought that he received the tapes in March 2002. It may well be that transcripts could have taken that length of time to be prepared.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you have your own independent recollection of what actually happened or do you only have your assumptions; i.e., that you assume that you were the one who provided him with the tape of that interview?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: My light is flashing. No objection but the reference to this topic is -- if it helps my friend, is on page 163 at the top.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: The second interview?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: The second interview, sorry, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The 11th March one, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Let's then look at that. You have page 163 before you. Look at the second interview. And please look at the lines from 1 through 4 or even through 7 on page 163 of that second interview.

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've got that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It arises from this, that you never provided Mr. Borovcanin with the tapes. [In English] You would copy tapes. [Interpretation] Do you have a takeover record? Did Mr. Borovcanin ever sign a receipt confirming that he received those tapes from you? Because it doesn't arise clearly from the transcript that this ever took place.

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not in personal possession of it. If there is one it will be within the Tribunal's system, and I would not be able to recall whether I handed it, the tapes, to Mr. Borovcanin or to his lawyer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Again we will not insist. If you can't remember, I will not go on insisting. I would like to ask you to look at page 2 of the transcript of this interview, the second interview. I believe that you have it before you now.

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And here you see the caution addressed at Mr. Borovcanin. That's on page 2 of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, we had an occasion on the examination-in-chief to hear that although at the beginning of this caution you told Mr. Borovcanin that he was a possible suspect, the way that was interpreted to him was "a suspect." Do you remember on chief Mr. Nicholls pointed to that fact, that this is how the things transpired during the interview?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe from yesterday there were different words used on different occasions, I'm not sure which occasion you're talking to, talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's a very pertinent remark that he's made to you, Mr. Lazarevic. I think you need to be specific, more specific.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, sir. Let me draw your attention to this. It's page 2 of the transcript you have before you. Lines 7 to 14. You have the English version before you now. I will be reading the B/C/S transcript. That is what Mr. Borovcanin heard, to show you my point. "Pursuant to information available to the Tribunal, the Prosecutor of the Tribunal believes you to be a suspect for certain acts that the Tribunal is concerned with. Therefore, before I ask you any questions, I have to advise you of your rights. You have rights because it is believed that you may, that you are a possible suspect." I have been reading from the B/C/S transcript. Now, you have this text in front of you.

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have an English version which differs -- is not absolutely identical.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Precisely. Precisely. That's my point. But what is really important to me is what kind of caution Mr. Borovcanin received. I am not trying to say that you deliberately fell short in any way in giving that caution. I just want to draw everyone's attention to what Mr. Borovcanin actually heard as caution. Now, you are looking at the English text. Mr. Borovcanin was told by you, "a possible suspect," but the translation he received from the interpreter, the word "possible" is missing. So he heard in translation that "he was a suspect." Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, if that's what the translation was.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: My impression that that is not -- not only is not being contested by the Prosecution, but it was pointed out -- specifically pointed out by the Prosecution themselves. So can you go straight to what you wish to get the witness to state?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can I draw your attention, Mr. Lazarevic, to line 9 of previous page, page 12, what you read from the B/C/S transcript was translated by the interpreters as "a possible suspect as well." Is it correct or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, precisely, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So my point concerning is this -- actually I'm going to put it to the witness now. The second part of the caution, where you again say to Mr. Borovcanin that he may be a suspect and the interpreter interprets that correctly, in the next sentence, however, Mr. Borovcanin hears that he is at once "a possible suspect" and at the same time "a suspect." Do you agree that that's what he heard?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not contesting it. What I would say is that is not the caution. That is explaining why I'm going to give the caution. The caution is actually the next section.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lazarevic, sorry for that interruption. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I will proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one more question regarding the interview of the 11th of March 2002, now I'm only talking about the 11th. Although the interview continued on the 12, I'm only concerned with the 11th. Throughout that interview, did the counsel, the lawyer, Goran Bubic, legal representative of Mr. Borovcanin, utter a single word apart from introducing himself for the benefit of the audio recording?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: Without checking the transcript, I couldn't be certain, but if his name is not mentioned in the transcript, then he will not have said anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Nicholls, would you be prepared to stipulate what is being suggested by Mr. Lazarevic? Otherwise we would have to give Mr. Graham the opportunity to skim through the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I don't think it's a huge point, but I think on the 11th and the 12th counsel did speak during the interview.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I don't think we are going to have a huge argument.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You're not prepared to stipulate. So, Mr. Graham, if you so wish, you can take your time to go through the transcript and confirm or contest the proposition that was put to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, maybe I can be of assistance. There is a search engine that can deal with it within a minute. This interview is on 100 pages. I really don't want to take time away from the Trial Chamber. I think that can be done very quickly and then if the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I do appreciate your comments and your suggestion, Mr. Lazarevic, but on the other land, do you really need the witness to confirm to you if Mr. Bubic 1, or Mr. Bubic 2, whoever it was, intervened at any time apart from saying good morning or good afternoon or my name is Zoran or Goran Bubic? Can't you prove that through the transcript itself?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I may be able to shorten it. I see on page 160 and 161 there is some discussion of how documents will be exchanged. So technically it's -- I don't think it's a huge point but it is -- I can't stipulate that he didn't say anything other than hello.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I understand that, Mr. Nicholls. On the other hand I don't think we need questions to establish what we can actually look at and find out ourselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Then I will skip this subject altogether. I just wanted to draw the attention of the Chamber to certain facts that are pertinent to my argument.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Graham, could we now look at page 115 of the interview? That's the interview of the 12th of March 2002. If you had a look at the transcript, it's line 10 on page 115 of the transcript. Mr. Nicholls did not deal with this yesterday. But in the version that is agreed between us and the Prosecution, it says that Mr. Borovcanin did not hear the interpretation of the following sentence: "In this interview, your rights remain exactly the same." Can you confirm that this is in the transcript?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. At the very end of this interview, on the 12th, Mr. Borovcanin, if you remember, raised the issue again of getting the tapes of those interviews. And as we had occasion to see a minute ago, you had this conversation about securing tapes for Mr. Borovcanin, he was told he would get them ASAP. We are now talking specifically about the tapes of the 11th and 12th of March interviews.

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I ask which page of the transcript we are looking at?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: That's the page of the transcript -- the last page of the transcript, 163, the first line, you are speaking.

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm that now?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The Defence of Mr. Borovcanin asserts that the tapes of these interviews of the 11th and 12th of March 2002 were not received by him before he arrived here in The Hague at the Detention Unit. Do you allow for that possibility?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no knowledge either way. I will certainly allow for it, but I have no knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. It's all right, sir. If you don't know, you don't know. If you have that interview in front of you, look at page 162, please. An offer was made to Mr. Borovcanin that in case something remained unclear during the interview, or if he believed he needed to reanswer a question, he could contact the Office of the Prosecutor and a new interview would be organised. Can you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe it says the best way to do it is for his lawyer to contact our office.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You see, I have to tell you that I did not calculate very precisely how long all these interviews with Mr. Borovcanin took. I used a rough estimate made by my colleagues from the OTP, but it is a total of about 15 hours. Is that consistent with what you remember? Does that sound correct? Around 15 hours?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really have never sat and added it up. If the -- if that's the fact, then, yes. The start and finish times are all there to be calculated, but I've never done that. I'm not disputing it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: But you do remember that there were several interviews, each one lasting several hours?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a long interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And that is precisely my point. Do you believe that in view of all of that, Mr. Borovcanin would have been able to remember precisely each question and each answer he gave during the interview without listening to the tapes to jog his memory?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sure he would not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I suppose that your experience includes using cassette recorders and that dubbing involves connecting two tape recorders, pressing play on one recorder, pressing record on another recorder, and the recording takes exactly the same amount of time as the tape is long. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: For copying one tape to the other, I believe the Tribunal had a fast copying machine but I'm no expert.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. But let's take it even that there wasn't one. The dubbing takes as much time as the tape is long. What would therefore be the reason for not making copies for Mr. Borovcanin?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean copies on -- at the location at the time?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Certainly not, because I can't even assume that you had two tape recorders at the location at the time, but within the next couple of days was it possible, physically possible, to do that?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a procedure in place within the Tribunal for copying tapes such as these. They had to be entered into the evidence unit and it then passed out of my hands. I would not be responsible for copying.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you very much. I have two more questions to end with. Before Mr. Borovcanin provided the interview, he did not take a solemn declaration to say that he would speak the truth and nothing but the truth; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: My last question: After the end of the interview, Mr. Borovcanin did not sign a receipt, a confirmation, or an affidavit that he had spoken the truth and nothing but the truth during the interview in the same fashion as the witnesses do here in the proceedings before this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: He had not signed, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I have no further questions for you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you so much, Mr. Lazarevic. Who wishes to go next? I have on my list the Beara Defence team, the Popovic Defence team, the Miletic -- and the Miletic Defence team.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: We will not cross-examine this witness Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Merci, Mr. Zivanovic. Mr. Meek? Will you be cross-examining the witness, Madam Fauveau?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Probably, Mr. President, for about ten minutes or so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. You asked for 30 minutes, Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. I'm hearing things again, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] [Microphone not activated] [B/C/S coming over English channel].

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: We are hearing Serbian, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The problem seems to be the following: That my microphone registers as off when it is on. And secondly, whatever I am saying very rightly so is being translated into Serbo-Croat. But that's what I am receiving myself, which shouldn't be the case. Have you been receiving the interpretation in Serbo-Croat? You have. So there is an overlapping between the two channels, the Serbo-Croat channel and the English channel. With regard to the French, Madam Fauveau? Are you receiving interpretation in French?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am indeed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. I think it may have been fixed from what I can gather. Mr. Meek, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm sure you understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Very understanding, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Graham, how are you?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fine, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Chris Meek and I represent Ljubisa Beara. I have a few questions for you. First is on the first interview, February 20th, 2002, on page 2, you're talking to Mr. Borovcanin about the fact that he has a right to be assisted by legal representative or a lawyer, page -- line 20, correct, do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: In fact my papers have become mixed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: If it helps we can replace the entire set.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I have it setup, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's all sorted out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Nicholls, any way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. Graham, if you would just take the time to read to yourself lines 20 through 24, I would appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Now, do you have any specific recollection of after you advised Mr. Borovcanin of the fact that he had the right to a lawyer in this interview, that he responded to you, "Yes," that he understood, "I told you that already. He can join us later." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, do I.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Can you tell this Tribunal, please, this Chamber, when it was that you had discussions with Mr. Borovcanin prior to turning the tape recorder on the 20th day of February 2002 at approximately -- I don't even see the time but that morning or afternoon?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: When Mr. Borovcanin first arrived at the Banja Luka headquarters, I was -- I will have been waiting in the room and somebody would have come to tell me that he was here. I went out for people who were being interviewed. I always met them in the reception area and it will have been at that point that he told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Now, were you in the room by yourself or was Mr. Peter McCloskey with you in the room?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I met, first met Mr. Borovcanin, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Yes, you just described that you had been in a room, someone would have come and told you that the witness was there, the person being interviewed, and you said I went out and met him. My question to you: Were you with Peter McCloskey or not?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, myself, Mr. McCloskey and the interpreter will have been waiting in the interview room. At that point there will be no guarantee that Mr. Borovcanin was going to turn up. That was not uncommon, for people not to arrive.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: So I take it that the interpreter, Mr. McCloskey, and yourself were in the same room, but yet you only went out to talk to and meet with Mr. Borovcanin or did Mr. McCloskey go with you? That's my question.

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, Mr. McCloskey did not come with me. The interpreter will have come with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And how long did that conversation take place?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge it would be one or two minutes. It would be to introduce myself, the fact that Mr. Borovcanin had a lawyer who was not there would have been mentioned, and then we would have gone down to the interview room.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Yesterday you were shown the summons that was sent to Mr. Borovcanin. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And in that summons, it's stated that he had the status of a suspect. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Then again, how long have you been a law enforcement officer?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: I joined the police in 1985, in the U.K.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: So by the time you did this interview you'd been a law enforcement officer for approximately 17 years, correct?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And you are very aware of the importance of a person who the government or in this case the Office of the Prosecutor claims to be a suspect to have the right to an attorney if he's going to be questioned, don't you, sir?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm well aware of yeah, the importance of somebody that's going to be questioned as a suspect. The term "suspect" is different in different jurisdictions, I presume.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Well, let me just ask you this, Mr. Graham. What did you presume that it meant on the 20th day of February 2002?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: I presumed it fitted in with the definition that I could not quote off-hand, now after being out of the Tribunal for so long, but he fitted the criteria for being a suspect; and therefore should be afforded the rights to be given to somebody of such a status.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And it's your testimony under oath that you met with him and he told you that, "I have a lawyer, but he will be coming later because he's tied up in court"?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's my recollection, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And, sir, the only reason I'm pausing is because we both speak English, and I'm trying to wait until the cursor stops so that the interpreters don't get upset with us. Now, did you, sir, being an experienced police officer, and knowing the importance of a person being -- having the status of a suspect, having legal counsel present, and specifically one who has told you he has legal counsel present, did you explain to Mr. Borovcanin that you did not need to start the interview and should not start the interview until his lawyer arrived?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, if to the best of my recollection, yes, I told him we did not need to start the interview. I do not recall and do not imagine that I did not tell him we do not need to start the interview. That was up to him. I gave him a very clear opportunity to start or not to start and to postpone any way through whenever he felt was necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Did you take the time to advise him that in his position, if you were him, you would wait for the lawyer?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: The advice that I gave him is on the tape, and I was certainly not taking putting myself the position of being a lawyer and giving him legal advice. I just told him as it was, it's all on the tape exactly what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. Graham, maybe I've been unclear. We haven't even got to the taped interview. I'm talking about when you met him outside and it wasn't taped and he told you he had a lawyer, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: My friend is not being clear. I think he's correct on that because Mr. Graham has already discussed the nature of that conversation, I won't say in front of the witness exactly how he described it, but he's described what happened outside the -- in the reception room and how long it lasted and Mr. Meek is trying to make that into a long conversation where there is no evidence of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek. Why don't you go straight to the point?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Okay. I'll do that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Again, Mr. Graham, with all your experience and training and you've testified the importance of a person like this having an attorney, why didn't you tell him he should not start the interview until his lawyer came?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think he's answered that question. According to him that would have been the proper thing for a lawyer to do, and he was not filling that role.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's how I got it. So let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Did you have any discussions with the senior legal adviser, Peter McCloskey, who was present with you about this situation of Mr. Borovcanin showing up having a lawyer but his lawyer not being present since Mr. McCloskey was a lawyer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Are you in or out now, Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Your Honour, at any time between the time Mr. Graham says he met Mr. Borovcanin outside and before the interview started, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Before the interview started. He's already told you that Mr. McCloskey was not with him at the time. He was with the interpreter at the time. So Mr. McCloskey couldn't have said anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Let me clarify that if I might.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: You had this discussion with the interpreter and Mr. Borovcanin. You walked inside. Am I correct so far?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And at that point, you were in the room with Mr. Borovcanin, Mr. McCloskey, the interpreter and yourself. The four of you, correct?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Before the tape recorder was turned on, did you tell Mr. McCloskey, take him aside or even in front of Mr. Borovcanin, Peter, he has a lawyer but his lawyer is not going to be here. What should we do? You're a lawyer, I'm not. Did you ever have that sort of conversation?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not recall any conversation with Mr. McCloskey. I will have gone in and pointed out the fact that Mr. Borovcanin was here without his lawyer, and his lawyer was at court and coming later. There was no discussion about -- that I recall about how to continue. It then went on to the tape which is standard procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Sir, may I ask you in your experience in law enforcement and interviewing individuals, suspects, and potential suspects, do you prefer that they have lawyers or not have lawyers, as a law enforcement officer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I would say that was totally irrelevant to this hearing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I suppose you wish to respond to that or move to your next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I would like to respond to it. It goes to the -- this issue goes to the voluntariness, or if anything was coerced, then I think it's relevant as to whether or not this witness would have preferred to take this statement from Mr. Borovcanin with an attorney or without an attorney.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: He's just shown how totally irrelevant it is because what was going on in the investigator's mind is -- has got nothing to do with the way the interview was conducted. It doesn't matter what he preferred about attorneys, what he preferred to have for lunch that day. We've got the tape recording exactly the interview started. My friend's -- of everything that happened during the interview, and my friend has just gone through what happened before the interview.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Meek, please proceed to your next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Sir, you flew in on last Saturday to testify; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Where did you fly in from, sir?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: Manchester, England.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And yesterday you said that the first opportunity you had to actually read a version of the transcript was on your flight over, is that true, sir?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: By that I mean I looked at it in the airport in Manchester, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And did you read it all?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: I skimmed read it. I wasn't in a position to read it all in detail at that stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Okay. And so yesterday when you said you actually read the version of it, today you're saying you skimmed it; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I read through it. But if you'd asked me detailed questions on it, I would have struggled. One of the issues that I had was the font that I'd been able to print it out in. Did not have the times PP font, so a great many of the words did not make any sense to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Now, also, in going back briefly, let me ask you, sir, you knew because of the summons Mr. Borovcanin was a suspect. Can you tell me, please, why it was that you kept telling him, when you were reading him his so-called rights, that he was a possible suspect?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I think if I recall, Your Honour's grounds rules for this hearing was that everybody would have a chance to cross on the limited issues we had here, but there would not be repetition of the same questions and the same topics by all council which is what my friend is doing. This was gone over in direct and also obviously in cross-examination in quite a bit of detail.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He did answer it yesterday, so it's perfectly legitimate for you, Mr. Meek, to refer to that part of his testimony, and if you need any clarification, you will proceed along those lines. But not to repeat the same question, the same question that was already answered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Go straight to the --

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Let me rephrase it, Judge. I don't believe it's the same question but I'll rephrase it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: You testified yesterday that one of your colleagues who had been an investigator with the Office of the Prosecutor gave you a sheet of paper and that's what you read from, correct?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's actually a document that was on the OTP system, under one of the electronic files. He advised me where it was. I've got a hard copy of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And if I understand you correctly, that hard copy had the word "You are considered to be a possible suspect," and that's why you read it, correct?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: But you were a police officer for 17 years before you took this, and you knew that Mr. Borovcanin was actually a suspect. So my question is why didn't you tell him that instead of just read from that document when you knew that document wasn't correct?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was a police officer in England working under the laws and procedures of England for the period you're talking about. I was working under the laws and procedures of the Tribunal, and this was a document that was being used by the investigators within the Tribunal. I used it in good faith, and I have no reason to question it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: So if I understand you correctly, even though you knew Mr. Borovcanin was a suspect, you were going -- you were willing to tell him he was a possible suspect because you didn't want to question some supposed ICTY procedure, is that your answer, sir?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Okay. Then you had a senior trial attorney or senior trial adviser, Mr. McCloskey, with you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Mr. Meek, do you wish to explain any further? Because I think you were stopped right before you started to explain further.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I absolutely did not -- I think you said I was willing to tell him he was"a possible suspect," because I didn't want to tell him that he was actually a suspect. That is not the case at all. All the way through the interviews, I was trying to be totally fair and honest and find the truth. There was no intention or plan or -- to mislead or misinterpret anything. I thought I was being perfectly clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Let me -- in your last answer let me ask you if I understand it correctly. You were -- you thought you were being perfectly -- I'm sorry, perfectly clear in telling Mr. Borovcanin he was a possible suspect when you knew he was a suspect; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: I used the terminology to try and explain to Mr. Borovcanin that he had certain rights, and this was the reason I was giving him those rights. The right with regards to the caution with regards to having a lawyer present. So it was an explanation to him of why I was giving him those rights whereas many of the people I interview as witnesses did not have those rights.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Well, many people you interview as witnesses, excuse me, strike that, I'll start over. Witnesses being interviewed are different than suspects being interviewed, aren't they, sir?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly. That's why I was -- what I was trying to explain to him, there was a reason for giving him those rights.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Do you believe or excuse me, are you saying under oath that you thought you were being fair and above board when you told him he was considered a possible suspect when you knew he was considered a suspect?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes? Mr. Nicholls?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Asked and answered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And I'll make the point. I don't think there is any need to continue to repeat "under oath." Everybody knows who is under oath. It's just a -- there is no jury here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Skip that. We all do it, Mr. Nicholls. Although sometimes I agree it maybe redundant. Yes, Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I'm -- Judge, I don't think he's answered the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He's more than answered it, and he's answered it about six times already.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Now, you testified yesterday that the purpose of the interview was to establish where Mr. Borovcanin was and what happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You want the reference, Mr. Nicholls?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: No objection, just a reference, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Page 66 lines 24, 25, page 67, lines 1 and 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I will read it to what you your answer was: Answer: "I don't recall that being put as a direct question during the interviews, but the purpose of the interview was to establish where Mr. Borovcanin was and what happened. That was the purpose of the interview." Do you recall that, sir?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recall correctly that was in answer to a question about the specific crimes or acts being put to Mr. Borovcanin in the interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Well, I'm asking you was that the sole purpose of the interview, just to establish where Mr. Borovcanin was and what happened?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: The purpose, the complete purpose of the interview, I was going through as it -- it's self explanatory really. I went through the -- his background, his CV, and then the events in and around Srebrenica, and my primary role was to go through a chronology of those events.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Now, you'll agree with me, won't you, sir, that during the interview on the 20th of February 2002, and the further interview on 11th of March 2002, that Mr. Peter McCloskey from the Office of the Prosecutor asked the majority of the questions to Mr. Borovcanin?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: So I will ask you, if you know if your purpose was, as you just explained, what was the purpose of Mr. McCloskey's questions for Mr. Borovcanin? If you know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: The relevance of this to the voluntariness of the interview is completely escapes me. If the interview ends up being admitted and Mr. Graham testifies, which will be brief, about parts of the interview and how it's handled, then questions that go -- that may be relevant at that point can be put. But the basis of this hearing, I don't think dissecting all of this has any relevance whatsoever to the issues which we have to resolve on its admissibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What's your comment on that and please answer limitedly to the admissibility aspect that is being raised by Mr. Nicholls, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Your Honours, if you say I can't ask the question, I'll proceed. I think it's relevant, but if you don't then I won't proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We had some doubts, but I think it's clear now in our minds now and it's unanimous. We have no doubt in our mind that this has got nothing to do with admissibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We were going to say you're welcome, Mr. Meek, but I don't -- go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Would you agree with me, Mr. Graham, that in interviews such as these, when you start to give warnings to the people being interviewed, that the mistake of one word or two words can be very important?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it depends on the words and the context.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: All right. Well, let me ask you this: If you had dealt -- and you have, I'm sure, in your 17 odd years or now 20 years, 22 years, as a police officer, with people who have never come across and been entangled in the criminal justice system, and they become a suspect, and they're told that they have a right to an attorney, and they have a right not to be -- not to answer questions but if they do, anything they say can be used in a court of law and that person is a lay person; would you deem it important that they were not told that whatever they said would be used against them?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Trying to make sure I understand. Is he saying that based on the fact that he's been a policeman for 15 years, 20 years, that he knows about the rights and the obligations and the way the system works with all suspects being interviewed and that therefore a policeman should know and would know these things? Because if he is, then it's irrelevant in putting this to Mr. Borovcanin who is also a policeman for the same amount of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Nicholls. As I understand Mr. Meek, and Mr. Meek, I stand to be corrected if I misrepresent what you said, Mr. Meek's question is the following: Mr. Graham, given your extensive experience, given the common knowledge that we are dealing with a layman and not a -- someone conversant with the law, do you give any weight to the fact that when your statement, your caution, is being translated to him, the words "against you" are omitted? Is -- did I represent your question right, Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: You did, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, do you wish to comments now on it, Mr. Nicholls?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: No, if he's asking it in a vacuum context it has nothing to do with this interview, then I guess don't object. However, I will point out that it's also irrelevant to the extent that those words are not part of our warning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That aspect can become a submission later. For the time being it's being put as a proposition. It's being put as a proposition to the witness. And please keep in mind, Mr. Meek, the question that I put to the witness myself yesterday, whether he was aware that those words were not translated, whether he was aware at the time that those words were not translated to the witness, and he told us that he wasn't; he only became aware of that now. So what he can answer you now is how he feels about this whole affair now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Well, no, I understand that he doesn't speak B/C/S, and he didn't know it until now. But that begs the question -- I just wanted --

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Do you understand the question?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: The fact that the words "against you" were omitted?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course those words should have been used, the jurisdiction that I currently work in use the precise words of the caution, you have to make sure the person understands what you're actually telling them and then it becomes a matter of law.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Yeah. And it's also important, is it not, that -- and again, bearing in mind your expertise, so to speak, your years of experience as a law enforcement officer, that when you go to interview a suspect and he -- the person, he or she is a suspect, they should be clearly told that they're a suspect and not a possible suspect; do you agree with that, sir?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I've answered that question. It depends on the law enforcement area you're working in, and I was working within the laws and procedures of this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Any further questions, Mr. Meek? Because it's break time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Your Honour, I see it's time for the break. I may have a few questions after the break is all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So we'll have a 25-minute break starting from now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. Graham, yesterday, upon questioning by Mr. Lazarevic, and for the -- everybody here it would be on page 74 of yesterday's transcript, lines 2 through 7, but previously to your answer, he had asked you if you had ever told his client that he was free to leave the room, specifically, and I think your answer was, again from page 74 of yesterday's transcript, line 2, "When I'm reminding Mr. Borovcanin of his rights, I do tell him you do not have to answer any of your questions, if you want to, in terms of telling him he's free to leave the room. As I say, as an investigator I would have no power of arrest and that would be just arresting somebody. He's been out on a fresh air break so it didn't seem something I needed to say at that stage." Do you recall that, sir?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And that was the fresh air break on February 20th, when you stopped the interview at 10.27 a.m. and started it again at 15 minutes later, at 10.42 a.m. Do you recall that, sir? And if you're looking for it it's in the first interview, page 23, is where the interview continues, at 10.42 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think I state that in my opening lines of that tape.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Do you have any independent recollection of that?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Okay. Did you make any notes on this interview?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that I recall, certainly not any detailed notes and none that I kept. I was relying totally on the interview tape.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: So If you did take notes, you destroyed them? Is that what you're saying, sir?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't keep them. It was not normal practice to keep them. It was with the interview, and I certainly wouldn't have made notes of anything happening between -- in the breaks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: So when you say you didn't keep them, you destroyed them or through them away or did you leave them in a file here in the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they would have been shredded along with the interpreter's notes at the time which was policy, but do I not recall making any notes. I'm surmising if I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Do you recall whether or not you and Mr. McCloskey went outside on this short break to get fresh air and smoke a cigarette, perhaps?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: If I may -- where are we going?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Well, just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I hope not to smoke a cigarette.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Did you and Mr. McCloskey go outside and smoke a cigarette?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: That's not what I asked, Judge. Let me rephrase it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's what you asked actually, Mr. Meek, but you're free to rephrase it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Let me rephrase it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: You indicated that Mr. Borovcanin did go outside, correct?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the recollection I'm going off the tape, we had breaks and I'm stating there on the tape that we've had a break for fresh air.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Do you have any independent recollection of whether you and/or Mr. McCloskey went outside and were next to or close to Mr. Borovcanin during that break?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no recollection, but I would not have stayed close to Mr. Borovcanin, particularly -- I certainly would not have had any conversation with him whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Was there any times during these interviews when you were not having conversations with Mr. Borovcanin, but during breaks of any length of time you and Mr. McCloskey would be talking to each other in English and be close enough where he could hear you?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not recall any, but Mr. Borovcanin from my recollection spoke some English so --

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: That's correct. So my question is did you recall having any conversations with Mr. McCloskey to the effect that maybe it would help Mr. Borovcanin if he would be a more open or tell the truth such that he could hear you say such things?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I want to take you to the end of that interview on the 20th of February 2002, and you might find it on page 89. And Mr. Graham, really my pages are a little different. But it's the very end of that interview, the last three pages of the first interview. While you're looking for it, I'm not sure that you really need it, but you say that the tape is about to finish, time is 1715, being 5.15 in the afternoon, I'll just turn and put a new tape in straight away. You see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And then, on down, you state -- the next thing that is stated on this transcript and on the tape would be you saying, "Time is now 1740 on Wednesday, the 20th of February 2002"?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: This is the then continuing for most of the day with Mr. Borovcanin. You say, "If I can just confirm Mr. Borovcanin, when the last tape finished, we were planning to carry straight on. However, it was decided that senior trial attorney Mr. McCloskey should have a brief chat with your lawyer, Mr. Bubic, and so to avoid any complications, you were asked that you were not present while they had a legal consultation; is that correct? Do you recall saying that, sir?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's on the tape.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Do you recall saying it?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall those exact words, no, but I'm happy that's what I said because it's on the tape.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Do you remember that 25-minute break?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember the incident, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And where were you, sir? Were you out with Mr. McCloskey and Mr. Bubic?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not. I remained in the interview room with Mr. Borovcanin, and I believe the interpreter.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: All right. So no interpreter went out with Mr. McCloskey and Mr. Bubic?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could you please slow down for the interpreters?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Did you hear that, Mr. Meek? The interpreters would like to you slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I apologise to the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And that applies to you as well, Mr. Graham. Please don't overlap between question and answer. Allow a short pause.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not recall if the interpreter remained or went out with Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: You don't recall -- according to your testimony earlier today, I believe, you don't recall that either one of these lawyers named Bubic spoke any English; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which is why I do not recall whether the interpreter went out or did not go out. I assume if Mr. Bubic did not speak English then the interpreter will have gone out, but I have no direct recollection after this length of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Well, do you have any direct recollection of sitting in a room with Mr. Borovcanin for 25 minutes just the two of you?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember remaining in the room. And I'm not sure that this was even the only occasion that happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: You mean there were more occasions where Mr. McCloskey deemed it necessary to have a brief chat with Mr. Borovcanin's lawyer outside the presence of Mr. Borovcanin?

utterances.speaker: ALISTAIR GRAHAM [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There were more occasions where there was a break for some of these tapes. I could not tell you precisely at exactly which breaks Mr. Borovcanin left the room, remained in the room. All I can tell you is that, as is confirmed on the tapes, he was not asked any questions and there was no interview during those breaks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Sir, you say on the tape that while you had planned to carry straight on, that it was decided that Peter McCloskey should have this chat with lawyer Bubic. Can you tell me, sir, who decided this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I haven't objected up until now, but I don't see what this is relevant to as far as admissibility. I don't see what -- he -- he hasn't tied this up into any relevant legal issue and certainly not any legal issue he's advised us of. We were limited to the issues which were discussed on the 28th of June, that Mr. Lazarevic outlined, and I just don't see where this is going. He's talking about a discussion that -- between two attorneys. That has nothing, again, to do with the issue before us now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek? Could you respond to that, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Yes, I'd like to respond, Your Honour. The fact is I think that it may very well have relevance to the issue of voluntariness, coerciveness, and whether this should be admitted against Mr. Borovcanin because you see this was the end of the first interview and it stopped immediately thereafter. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic representing his client went through his entire cross-examination and there was no attack whatsoever in the integrity of the Prosecution, of Mr. McCloskey, of Mr. Graham, or of anybody involved. Mr. Lazarevic has confirmed to us that he is not alleging that there was ever at any time any coercion, any improper behaviour of that kind whatsoever during any of these interviews with his client. Now, if that's his position, his client, there is no foundation, there is no way that Mr. Meek can go on this fishing expedition. He's got no foundation for it whatsoever. He's just going through this speculative trawling exercise in the hopes of finding some way to call Mr. -- the STA as a witness. It's got no relevance, it's got no foundation, he should not be allowed to continue down this path.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek, how do you tie up the conversation that apparently took place between Mr. McCloskey and Mr. Bubic, whichever one of them it was, with the question of voluntariness and coercion?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If the rest of the transcript, what the rest of the transcript indicates is that the conversation was in the direction of stopping the interview for the day so that the interviewee would have an opportunity to consult with his lawyer, Mr. Bubic. And because of that, the interview came to an end on that day. So how do you tie it up with what you referred to as voluntariness and coerciveness? I use coercion but --

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I see that Your Honour has read the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We have it here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Yes, of course. The other question I have is I think the objection of the Prosecutor went to my standing to ask these questions more so than what -- where I was going with it. But if they want to -- let me answer if I might, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: If they want to and they've told you and they've told us, they want this interview admitted and they want it admitted against not only the maker but everybody else, and I submit to Your Honours that if something was all of a sudden there is a 25 minute break and Your Honour must feel that it was only about whether we should stop for the day or not, then I should be able to ask this witness what he knows about what they talked about if anything and why they took the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But then put that question and not the question that you put before.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But, however, one moment, Mr. Nicholls. You have not reflected correctly the essence of what Mr. Nicholls pointed out to you. What he pointed out to you is the following. We have listened to two hours plus of cross-examination by the Borovcanin Defence team, at no point in time was it hinted in the least that there was even the slightest measure of coercion, and you're being taken to task on this. If that is the position taken by the Borovcanin Defence team on behalf of their client, how do you then move a step further and tie up the -- what we have with the notion of coercion? If there is no allegation of coercion from the person who is most interested in this?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, we certainly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, the only information that -- Mr. Meek, sorry, the only information that transpires out of the relevant part of the transcript is that there was indeed a conversation between Mr. McCloskey and one of the Bubics, as a result of which once the interview was started again, it was pointed out that discussions had been held as a result of which it was felt appropriate that the interview will not proceed on that day and that rather the interviewee would have full opportunity to consult with his lawyer. That is what you have. There is no indication from anyone or anything else that what appears in the transcript is not truthful or faithful to what was stated and what was audio recorded. That's the position. So our question to you is: How do you relate this to the admissibility of the statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: First off, Your Honour, as you stated, when they came back on the record, Mr. McCloskey did, in fact, talk about that they agreed that it would be appropriate to stop the interview at that time but before that Mr. McCloskey had told Mr. Borovcanin that, "Your lawyer and I were able to discuss your situation a little bit. As you know, he's new in, to the case. I think you would agree that we were appropriate and candid and good discussions." But how we would tie it to it is a relevancy or the issue in this hearing as to the second -- the March interview. Was what they discussed -- was what they discussed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, earlier on, I can quote chapter and verse, if I find it, yes. You said, "the fact is" -- that's page 41, lines 9 onwards,"the fact is I think it may very well -- it may very well have relevance to the issue of voluntariness coerciveness, so our question to you if -- is the following: If what transpires from the transcript is that supposedly Mr. McCloskey and Mr. Bubic came to an agreement that rather than proceeding with the interview, the interviewee at the time would have an opportunity to have consultations with his lawyers," how do you fit that either in the ambit of voluntariness or the related and more specific sphere of coercion? How do you fit this or your question with what I have just told you? Or what you yourself had stated? If you wish to --

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: No, I do wish to answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- or if you want to put another question, please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
